project: MP2026CSE86 - EEG & ECG Analysis of Physiological Differences Associated with Yoga Experience

resting.name: Resting State (Baseline)
resting.layman_summary: Baseline reference state with eyes closed. Moderate Alpha waves are present, heart rate sits at standard baseline (~78 bpm), and the autonomic nervous system is in neutral balance.

internal_concentration.name: Internal Concentration (Meditation)
internal_concentration.meaning: Inward focus on breath, stillness, & meditation
internal_concentration.layman_summary: The signature meditative state. Focus is directed inward. Frontal Theta waves increase while brain-heart coupling peaks (Index: 0.014). Vagal recovery activates, raising RMSSD to 87.9 ms as breathing smoothly regulates the heartbeat.

external_concentration.name: External Concentration (Sensory Focus)
external_concentration.meaning: Active attention directed at sensory tasks
external_concentration.layman_summary: Active engagement with external stimuli. Alpha waves suppress sharply (0.005) while fast Beta waves engage. Heart rate variability peaks dynamically (RMSSD reaches 111.1 ms) to provide maximum cardiovascular flexibility.

mind_wandering.name: Mind Wandering (Daydreaming)
mind_wandering.layman_summary: The mind is allowed to drift into spontaneous thoughts. Alpha waves rebound (0.010) as the brain's default mode network activates. Heart rate variability returns to baseline levels (RMSSD: 77.8 ms).

eeg_alpha_rel_mean.physiological_meaning: Relaxed Cortical Synchrony vs Task-Induced Desynchronization
eeg_alpha_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Alpha waves represent a calm, idling brain. Notice how Alpha drops by 50% during External Concentration (0.5%) because the eyes and brain are busy processing outside tasks. During Meditation (1.0%) and Daydreaming (1.0%), Alpha rebounds strongly.

eeg_theta_alpha_ratio.layman_interpretation: Lowest during Internal Meditation (4.49), showing a serene, disciplined mind with low cognitive friction. Rises highest during External Focus (7.34) when active mental processing is required.

coupling_neuro_cardiac_index.layman_interpretation: Measures how tightly brain waves and heart beats are synchronized. During External Focus, brain and heart decouple to handle sensory input (drops to 0.7). During Meditation, brain and heart lock into high harmonic resonance (1.4).

eeg_delta_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Slow delta waves are kept lowest during Internal Concentration (7.1%), proving that meditation is an alert, wakeful state rather than drifting into sleep.

eeg_theta_beta_ratio.layman_interpretation: Lowest and most stable during Internal Concentration (25.46), showing that meditative practice keeps fast, anxious beta spikes under tight regulation.

ecg_rmssd.physiological_meaning: Beat-to-Beat Vagal Tone & Dynamic Autonomic Range
ecg_rmssd.layman_interpretation: Beat-to-beat elasticity rises steadily from Resting (77.3 ms) to Meditation (87.9 ms) and peaks during External Focus (111.1 ms). The heart dynamically expands its beat variance to meet cognitive demands.

ecg_lf_hf_ratio.layman_interpretation: Lower values mean higher parasympathetic calming activity. During External Concentration (0.575), parasympathetic tone remains high to maintain calm focus under pressure.

ecg_pnn50.layman_interpretation: Measures what percentage of consecutive beats differ by more than 50 milliseconds. Rises from 16.9% in Resting up to 23.7% in External Focus, showing strong autonomic adaptability.

ecg_sdnn.layman_interpretation: Total heart rate variation spread expands from 55.6 ms at rest to 61.3 ms during meditation and 74.1 ms during active external attention.

coupling_alpha_rmssd_prod.layman_interpretation: Multiplies relaxed brain waves by heart elasticity. High during Internal Meditation (0.41) and Mind Wandering (0.48), but drops to 0.28 during External Focus when the brain desynchronizes to process outside tasks.

eeg_beta_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Remains tightly bounded at 0.4% across resting and meditative states, showing that meditative focus does not overload the cortex with excess cognitive noise.

ecg_hf.layman_interpretation: Parasympathetic rest-and-digest power peaks during focused states (78.8 to 80.4 ms²) and drops during Mind Wandering (71.6 ms²), indicating that daydreaming carries subtle autonomic instability.
